headline: EXPORT SALES AT 7:30; SOYOIL RUNS, CORN EASES
subheadline: Weekly export sales print at 7:30 AM CT; soybean oil leads the complex higher overnight while corn gives back a nickel on mid-season stress fears.
lead: Corn eased to $5.08 overnight as seed company commentary about warm-night yield drag circulates, and the market is positioning ahead of this morning's export sales at 7:30 AM CT. Soybeans are barely green at $12.53, holding gains from Wednesday's ratings-cut bid. Soybean oil ran 2.6% higher and is the one number worth watching before the report prints.
the_takeaway: Wait for 7:30; export sales decide whether beans hold $12.53 or give it back.
teaser: Export sales in 90 minutes. Soybean oil running. Corn soft on yield-stress chatter. Here is what matters.

one_number.context: Hard red winter wheat settled at $7.40, the highest close in six weeks. That is still below the $8 floor millers and feedlots watch, but the trend is putting that level back on the calendar.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans up toward $12.47; November beans closed at $12.63, well through the line.
yesterdays_call.note: Two straight hits on beans. The ratings-cut bid delivered. Now 7:30 decides the next leg.

sections.title: GRAINS: CORN SOFT, BEANS HOLD
sections.body:
- Corn at **$5.08** gave back nearly 5 cents as Renk Seed's Karl Bobholz flagged nearly a month of above-ideal overnight temperatures cutting into dough-stage starch fill across the Midwest, the kind of yield-drag commentary that travels fast before harvest data arrives.
- Soybeans at $12.53 are essentially flat, supported by short covering and late pod-fill weather uncertainty, but the real test is the export sales number at 7:30 AM CT: a soybean figure below 300K MT keeps the chart doing the work; above 500K MT and the China commitment gets another leg under it.
- December corn at $5.32 still sits above the $5.25 level this briefing flagged as the pricing window for unpriced new-crop; that window narrows each day harvest talk picks up.
sections.catalyst: Renk Seed commentary on warm overnight temps limiting corn yields in key Midwest areas.
sections.bottom_line: Corn's yield-drag story is real but unquantified; 7:30 export sales are the next hard data point.
sections.farmer_action: December corn at $5.32: if you have unpriced new-crop bushels, the window is still open but narrowing. Do not wait for combines.
sections.vs_yesterday: Corn: ratings-cut bid faded; yield-stress chatter replaced it overnight.

sections.title: SOYOIL BREAKS FROM THE COMPLEX
sections.body:
- Soybean oil at **$67.85** ran 2.6% overnight, the clearest move in the grain complex, while meal at $329.90 eased half a percent: that split says the bid is about crush product allocation, not raw bean demand.
- The biofuel coalition's push against expanded small refinery exemptions under the RFS is live in Washington today, and any erosion of SRE waivers tightens the soyoil demand floor for renewable diesel feedstock.
sections.catalyst: Biofuel coalition formally asking Trump not to expand Small Refinery Exemptions; RFS demand floor under soyoil.
sections.bottom_line: Soyoil running on RFS politics, not crop news; watch whether meal follows or the split widens.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRM, SCREWWORM CLOCK TICKING
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$220.30** firmed 0.8% and feeders at $333.80 added 0.4%; both contracts are recovering from Wednesday's slide, with the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ phased reopening still four days out and feeder supply still tight.
- The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for ivermectin injection against New World screwworm Thursday, the 14th EUA in the response, which is biosecurity infrastructure support ahead of the reopening date, not a cure for the supply-tightness story.
sections.catalyst: FDA Emergency Use Authorization for ivermectin against New World screwworm; Douglas port reopening Aug 24.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle bouncing on thin supply, not demand; the Douglas reopening pace next week is the real tell.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: double-hit narrative eased; screwworm EUA gives modest biosecurity support.

sections.title: CRUDE FIRMS ON VENEZUELA TALKS
sections.body:
- WTI at **$83.61** rose 2.2%, its sharpest session in weeks, as reports circulated that the Trump administration is in active talks to take direct US ownership stakes in Venezuelan oil fields, a supply-route story that the market is trading as a geopolitical premium rather than a near-term barrel change.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has since cooled with the premium deflating into August, remains the backdrop; Venezuela adds a second supply-uncertainty thread without changing the fundamental building-stock picture.
sections.catalyst: Reports of US-Venezuela talks over direct ownership of Venezuelan oil fields, adding geopolitical supply premium.
sections.bottom_line: Crude's 2.2% move is geopolitical positioning, not a supply signal; diesel input cost for fall fieldwork unchanged.

outside_the_pit.title: CHS and OCP Plan First US Phosphate Plant in 40 Years
outside_the_pit.body: CHS and Morocco's OCP announced a joint venture to build a one-million-metric-ton-per-year phosphate fertilizer facility in Louisiana, the first new US capacity in four decades. If it gets built, it restructures the import-dependency picture for DAP and MAP pricing by the late 2020s.

outside_the_pit.title: R-CALF Pushes Mandatory Country-of-Origin Labeling on Beef Imports
outside_the_pit.body: R-CALF USA is calling for M-COOL reinstatement after Trump's proclamation to expand foreign beef imports to lower retail prices. For cow-calf and fed-cattle producers, label origin is both a marketing tool and a packer-margin lever; the policy fight is now formally open.

weekly_thread.question: Does Crop Progress show eastern Corn Belt condition damage from Indiana's flooding, or does the crop hold ratings through late August?
weekly_thread.status_text: Monday's Crop Progress showed a ratings dip. Today's export sales at 7:30 AM CT are the next hard data point; the September WASDE is the next yield event.

the_more_you_know.title: The meal/oil split is the crush market's tell.
the_more_you_know.body: When soybean oil runs and meal lags, as happened overnight, the crush complex is pricing renewable-diesel feedstock demand above protein demand. At $67.85 oil versus $329.90 meal, the oil share of crush value is at its highest point in months. That ratio, not the bean price, tells you which side of the soy complex is doing the bidding right now.

watch_list.desc: USDA Weekly Export Sales: soybeans above 500K MT puts China commitment back in the conversation; below 300K MT and the chart holds the wheel.
Douglas, AZ phased cattle import reopening: feeder/live spread is the tell on how fast returning Mexican supply reprices the feeder board.
December corn above $5.25: pricing window for unpriced new-crop still open, but harvest-pressure talk is building.
Farm Bill revote expected in September after Senate Ag markup failed Aug 6; year-round E15 provision in the Senate text is a structural corn-demand tailwind if enacted.
